description: Use this when you need the true matches of a JavaScript regular expression rather than predicting regex behavior yourself, which is easy to get wrong. Deterministic: same input, same output. Returns every match with its index, length, matched text, positional capture groups (null for a group that didn't participate), and named groups (an object, or null when the pattern has none). Without the g flag only the first match is returned; with g all matches are collected, capped at 10,000 with truncated=true. Inputs are length-bounded (pattern 2,000 chars, text 50,000 chars) as a ReDoS guard. Example: pattern (?<y>\d{4})-(?<m>\d{2}) over "2024-01" with flag g -> matchCount 1, match "2024-01", groups ["2024","01"], named {y:"2024",m:"01"}.

flags.description: Any of g i m s u v y.

name: test_regex

flags.description: The flags applied (subset of g i m s u v y).

matchCount.description: Number of matches returned in the matches array.

matches.description: One entry per match, in order of appearance.

groups.description: Positional capture groups 1..n; a non-participating group is null.

index.description: Zero-based start offset of the match in the text.

named.description: Named capture groups as name->value, or null when the pattern defines none; a non-participating named group is null.

pattern.description: The regex source that was compiled (echoed back).

truncated.description: True if the 10,000-match cap was hit and further matches were dropped.
